summary: Index lists a Horetzky Fire Lookout pinned on Mount Horetzky north of Smithers, BC; no source found describes a tower there.

evidence.supports: index lists a Horetzky Fire Lookout
index places the entry in Bulkley-Nechako
peak north of Smithers, north side of the Babine River above Shanagh Creek
evidence.quote: N side of Babine River above Shanagh Creek, N of Smithers

notes_for_editor: Only one listing exists (Firelookout.ca slug horetzky-fire-lookout, id 13985). The listing has no tower type, year or height, and nothing else in the sources describes a structure. The pin lies within about 40 m (about 130 ft) of the official point of Mount Horetzky (my calculation from the two coordinate pairs), so the entry may have been named after the mountain rather than a surveyed structure. Two search results were not read and are not used: a 2016 provincial news release about a prescribed burn about 40 km north of Fort Babine, and a 2023 BC Wildfire Service bulletin mentioning a fire south of the mountain. Neither mentions a lookout. The namesake (the photographer Charles Horetzky) is not cited. Worth asking Recreation Sites and Trails BC or the BC Wildfire Service Northwest Fire Centre whether a tower ever stood on the summit. The story now uses the index's own wording, Bulkley-Nechako, instead of Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako, because the regional district label was not checked against a boundary source. The BC names record shows the status adopted and the date 1951-07-05 without a field label, so the story reports that date as the record's date rather than as a named decision date.
